title: Operator onboarding kickstart and telemetry contract for private deploys
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary:

This document is a kickstart playbook for operators taking ownership of a Redwood Private deployment (VPC or on-prem). It bundles a 30–90 minute onboarding checklist with a prescriptive telemetry contract that the operator and site reliability lead must implement before handoff. The goal is to provide a reproducible, minimal set of actions that guarantee observability, SLA evidence, and safe operator-run cutovers for initial production traffic.

Goals:
- Get an operator from zero to evidence-ready in a single shift (30–90 minutes depending on environment).
- Establish a minimum telemetry contract and SLIs for latency, availability, and errors.
- Provide clear acceptance criteria and escalation paths for first 72 hours of live traffic.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: Field operators, on-call SREs, professional services engineers, and customer platform engineers supporting a Private deployment.
- Scope: Initial provisioning validation, telemetry wiring and validation, basic responder-runbook, and acceptance criteria for operator sign-off. Not a complete hardening guide; see onprem-packaging and day-2-ops docs for deeper procedures.

Preflight checklist (must be completed before kickstart):
1. Access and identity
   - Operator has service account with least-privilege access to the runtime control plane and telemetry ingest (IAM role documented).
   - KMS/HSM credentials are present and testable via the provided CLI: `redwood-kms status`.
2. Networking
   - VPC routing established, health-check CIDRs whitelisted for Redwood control-plane probes.
   - Egress paths for telemetry and model artifact refresh verified.
3. Baseline artifacts
   - Model bundle installed and signature verified (sha256).
   - Runtime image and node OS image match approved hash.
4. Observability endpoints ready
   - Metric ingest endpoint reachable (https://ingest.example.local:443).
   - Tracing collector and log forwarding targets configured.

Kickstart procedure (30–90 minute rapid onboarding):
- Duration target: 30 minutes for validation in staging; 60–90 minutes for initial production handoff.

Step 0 — Gather:
- Operator machine with VPN access, kubeconfig (or runtime ctl), and telemetry write credential.

Step 1 — Smoke deploy and health checks (15 minutes)
1. Deploy a no-traffic canary: `redwoodctl deploy --profile canary --model small --replicas 1`
2. Verify pod/container runtime is `Running/Ready` and kernel logs show successful model load: `redwoodctl logs --tail 200`.
3. Confirm KV cache warmed (if used) via runtime metrics `runtime.kv_cache.populate_ratio`.

Step 2 — Telemetry wiring and verification (15 minutes)
1. Apply the telemetry config (example in Appendix).
2. Trigger synthetic requests (see synthetic harness snippet below) for 1 minute at a QPS of 0.5 to generate baseline traces and metrics.
3. Verify metric presence in the monitoring dashboard within 90 seconds and tracing spans appear in the tracing UI within 2 minutes.

Step 3 — SLI smoke and alert sanity (10 minutes)
1. Run SLI script to compute rolling 5m availability and median tail latencies: `scripts/sli_check.sh --window 5m`.
2. Confirm alerts are in a non-firing state or firing correctly for expected conditions (CPU throttle, missing model bundle).

Step 4 — Operator acceptance and signoff (5 minutes)
- Operator records timestamped evidence (screenshot or links) for: deploy success, telemetry channels populated, and SLI baseline within acceptable thresholds. Attach to the customer onboarding ticket.

Minimum telemetry contract (required fields & semantics)
- Reasoning: Private deployments must provide the same minimal visibility as Redwood hosted, so incident detection and billing traces are possible without exposing customer data.
- Contract guarantees: names, types, semantics, and retention required for metrics, traces, and logs.

Telemetry fields table (text table):
| metric_name | type | description | required | aggregation |
| runtime.request.count | counter | Per-route request count (incremented on request arrival) | yes | sum/1m |
| runtime.request.latency_ms | histogram | End-to-end server latency (ms) including queue time | yes | p50,p90,p99 |
| runtime.request.error | counter | Increment for all responses that map to 5xx or model-failure codes | yes | sum/1m |
| runtime.kv_cache.populate_ratio | gauge | Fraction [0..1] of KV cache that is warm for active models | recommended | latest |
| runtime.gpu.utilization_pct | gauge | Average GPU utilization per GPU device | recommended | p95 |
| runtime.node.health | gauge | 0 = unhealthy (not ready), 1 = healthy | yes | latest |
| runtime.model.version | tag/string | Model artifact semantic version for request routing | yes | N/A |

Required traces and span semantics:
- Root span: `request` with attributes: `route`, `model.version`, `tenant.id` (obfuscated/hashed for privacy), `request.size.tokens`, `response.size.tokens`, `replica.id`.
- Span completion must include `status.code` (OK | ERROR | TIMEOUT) and `error.message` only if non-sensitive (truncate or hash sensitive contents).

Logs and PII policy:
- Logs must not contain raw customer prompts or responses. All user-generated content must be redacted or sent through a PII scrubber before indexing. See data-management policy for allowed exception flows.

Retention and sampling policy (minimum baseline):
- Metrics: 90 days full-resolution (1m) stored; 13 months aggregated (daily).
- Traces: Full traces retained for 7 days. Traces sampled deterministically for error traces (100% of error traces), and probabilistically for successful traces at 5% by default.
- Logs: Error logs retained for 90 days. Access to raw logs is restricted and audited.

Sampling knobs (recommended):
- `trace.sampling.error = 1.0`
- `trace.sampling.success = 0.05`
- Ability to overrider per-tenant sampling for debug windows (operator-run only, must be timeboxed).

SLIs, SLOs, and burn rate decomposition (operator-facing):
- Availability SLI: requests with `status.code == OK` observed over rolling 5m window.
- Latency SLI: p95 of `runtime.request.latency_ms` for production routes.
- Default SLOs for new Private deployments (first 30 days):
  - Availability: 99.5% (rolling 30d)
  - Latency (p95): <= 600ms for typical small model routes; larger models should have documented baselines.
- Alerting: page at burn rate >= 2 for 15 minutes; ticket at burn rate >= 4 for 30 minutes.

Operator acceptance criteria (must pass before 1st customer cutover):
- Deploy smoke canary is running and healthy for 10 consecutive minutes.
- All required metrics are visible in the monitoring workspace and producing values.
- Trace root spans appear with the required attributes for at least 100 synthetic requests.
- Alerting rules are present and correctly resolved/non-firing for baseline synthetic traffic.
- Evidence artifact (links/screenshots, CLI outputs) are attached to onboarding ticket.

Common failure modes and mitigation (triage steps):
- Telemetry not appearing
  1. Check network egress firewall rules (port 443 to metric collector).
  2. Validate the telemetry credential: `curl -f -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" https://ingest.example.local/health`
  3. Inspect runtime logs for telemetry exporter errors `cat /var/log/redwood/telemetry.log | tail -n 200`
- Excess tracing volume causing cost spikes
  1. Immediately reduce `trace.sampling.success` to 0.01 and notify Redwood support.
- Model load failures after canary deploy
  1. Capture deploy logs, confirm model artifact signature, and revert to the last known-good model via `redwoodctl model rollback --to <sha256>`

Appendix — synthetic harness (example):
- Minimal Python snippet to generate synthetic traffic for verification:

```python
import requests
for i in range(100):
    r = requests.post('https://private-runtime.example.local/v1/generate', json={"prompt": "Hello world"}, timeout=5)
    print(r.status_code, r.elapsed.total_seconds())
```

Appendix — example telemetry config (YAML):

```
telemetry:
  metrics_endpoint: https://ingest.example.local:4318
  traces_endpoint: https://traces.example.local:4318
  logs_endpoint: https://logs.example.local:443
  sampling:
    error: 1.0
    success: 0.05
  credentials: /etc/redwood/telemetry/ingest-token
```

Appendix — ownership and escalation:
- Primary owner: Operator on-call (field operator team).
- Secondary owner: Private Deployments SRE (pager: private-sre, slack: #private-sre).
- Redwood platform escalation: domestic enterprise on-call (pager: redwood-enterprise).
- Escalation matrix: low (ticket) -> medium (page on-call) -> high (exec bridge).

References and related artifacts:
- See `private-deploy-operator-handshake-and-runtime-guardrails-2026` for runtime guardrails and hardened operator playbook.
- See `post-installation-telemetry-and-acceptance-checklist-2026` for full acceptance test vectors and evidence templates.
